concepts.title: Past Perfect and Past Continuous
concepts.definition: The past perfect (had + third form) names the earlier of two past actions. The past continuous (was or were + verb-ing) names an action going on at a past moment, often cut by a short event.
concepts.formula: earlier action: had + V3;  ongoing action: was/were + V-ing
concepts.key_idea: Two past events? The first one takes had + V3.
question_patterns: Fill in the blank with the past perfect form
Fill in the blank with the past continuous form
Complete the sentence with had + third form or was/were + ing

solution_steps.explain: the earlier action takes the past perfect (had + V3)
when + short event leaves the longer action in the past continuous

worked_examples.q: Fill in the blank with the past perfect form: The train ___ before we reached the station. (leave)
Fill in the blank with the past continuous form: She ___ dinner when the phone rang. (cook)
Fill in the blank with the past perfect form: They ___ the match before the rain started. (finish)
Fill in the blank with the past continuous form: I ___ my teeth when the doorbell rang. (brush)
Fill in the blank with the past perfect form: By the time we arrived, the show ___ (begin)
Fill in the blank with the past continuous form: The children ___ in the garden all evening. (play)
Fill in the blank with the past perfect form: He realized he ___ his wallet at home. (forget)

concepts.title: Active to Passive Voice: Past and Modals
concepts.definition: The simple past passive is was or were + third form. A modal verb keeps its base form and takes be + third form: must complete becomes must be completed.
concepts.formula: past: was/were + V3;  modal: modal + be + V3
concepts.key_idea: Match the passive helper to the active tense: past -> was/were, modal -> modal + be.
question_patterns: Change the sentence into the passive voice
Fill the passive verb form in the blank
Rewrite the active sentence in the passive

solution_steps.explain: simple past -> was/were; modal -> modal + be
adverbs and time words stay put

worked_examples.q: Change into the passive voice: The teacher praised the student. - The student ___ by the teacher. (praise)
Change into the passive voice: The committee approved the plan. - The plan ___ by the committee. (approve)
Change into the passive voice: The boys broke the window. - The window ___ by the boys. (break)
Change into the passive voice: The chief guest gave away the prizes. - The prizes ___ away by the chief guest. (give)
Change into the passive voice: You must complete the form. - The form ___ completed. (must)
Change into the passive voice: The hunters captured the leopard. - The leopard ___ by the hunters. (capture)
Change into the passive voice: Someone stole my bicycle last night. - My bicycle ___ stolen last night. (be)

concepts.title: Prepositions: Set Phrases
concepts.definition: Many adjectives and verbs are followed by one fixed preposition: fond of, afraid of, apologize for, congratulate on, insist on, depend on, succeed in. The pair must be learned together.
concepts.formula: fond of, afraid of, apologize for, congratulate on, insist on, depend on, succeed in
concepts.key_idea: The first word decides the preposition - memorize the pair, not the sentence.
question_patterns: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition
Complete the fixed phrase with its preposition
Choose the preposition that follows the adjective or verb

solution_steps.explain: adjective or verb fixed with a preposition
fond of, apologize for, insist on, succeed in
the pair must sound complete by itself

worked_examples.q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: She is fond ___ classical music.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He apologized ___ his mistake.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: I congratulated her ___ her success.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The child is afraid ___ the dark.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He insisted ___ paying the bill.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: We should not depend ___ others for everything.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: She succeeded ___ convincing the principal.
